name: Ndyuka-Trio Pidgin
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Huttar, George L. & Velantie, Frank J. (1997) Ndyuka-Trio Pidgin, in S. G. Thomason (ed.) Contact Languages: A Wider Perspective
earlier_scan.note: Sketch of the dormant trade pidgin exists in the Thomason volume; not openly online, stress statement not read

new_statements.quote: De Nederlandsche spelwijze is gebezigd; ĕ = stomme e, als in groote; ĭ = i als in ginds; ŏ = o als in hol.; de g is de Friesche of Duitsche g; accent, indien niet aangegeven, op voorlaatste lettergreep. Kal. = Kalienja (Karaïbisch).
new_statements.translation: Dutch spelling is used; ĕ = mute e, as in groote; ĭ = i as in ginds; ŏ = o as in hol; the g is the Frisian or German g; accent, where not indicated, is on the penultimate syllable. Kal. = Kalienja (Carib).
new_statements.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1908. Verslag der Toemoekhoemak-expeditie (Tumuc-Humac-expeditie). Leiden: E. J. Brill. Bijlage II, Taal. A. De 'handelstaal' der Joeka's met de Trio's en Ojana's, p. 204.
new_statements.locator: Bijlage II A, p. 204 (PDF page 253), transcription key immediately preceding section 'I. Lichaamsdeelen enz.'
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the 1908 vocabulary of the Ndyuka-Trio trade pidgin, word accent is treated as falling on the penultimate syllable by default; words that deviate are written with an acute accent on the stressed vowel (e.g. tiontión 'cough', final stress). This is a transcriber's convention over a ~15-page wordlist, not an analytic phonological rule, but it is a first-hand statement that penultimate accent is the unmarked case.
new_statements.exceptions: Non-penultimate accent is marked item by item with an acute in the list (e.g. tiontión); some penultimate items also carry a redundant acute (bárba, wákoe). No classes of exceptions are described.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited from Ndyuka and Trio speakers by expedition members (list compiled by Bisschop van Tuinen); de Goeje's 1906 key for his Indian-language lists warns that citation-form stress differs from connected speech. The modern sketch (Huttar & Velantie 1997) was not accessible and may supersede or qualify this.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1908 source calls the variety 'de handelstaal der Joeka's met de Trio's en Ojana's' (trade language of the Ndyuka with the Trio and Wayana), i.e. the same Ndyuka-Amerindian trade pidgin Glottolog files as ndyu1241 (Huttar & Velantie's 'Ndyuka-Trio Pidgin'); de Goeje notes it was also used with Wayana (Ojana). Data are early-20th-century citation forms recorded on the Tapanahoni/Paloemeu, not the 1970s rememberer data of Huttar.

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1908. Verslag der Toemoekhoemak-expeditie (Tumuc-Humac-expeditie). Leiden: E. J. Brill. Bijlage II, Taal. A. De 'handelstaal' der Joeka's met de Trio's en Ojana's, p. 204.

sources.note: Transcription key at the head of the pidgin wordlist, p.204: 'accent, indien niet aangegeven, op voorlaatste lettergreep' = accent, where not marked, is on the penultimate syllable; deviating items carry a written accent (e.g. tiontio'n 'cough').

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1906. Bijdrage tot de ethnographie der Surinaamsche Indianen. Internationales Archiv fuer Ethnographie XVII, Supplement. Leiden: Brill (transcription key pp.34-35; 'Handelsdialekt tusschen Aucaners en Indianen gebruikelijk' wordlist pp.109-111).
sources.note: General key for all the wordlists marks 'klemtoon' with a diacritic and warns (of the Indians) that stress in isolated citation differs from connected speech, so 'het zou voorbarig zijn een vaste regel op te stellen'; the short 1906 trade-dialect list itself (111 items) has no stress statement. Superseded by the 1908 list per de Goeje himself.
Nothing on phonology; cites only Ethnologue 18 and Meira & Muysken 2017.
